scope: data-only review of 10 selected revised or new pairs
dataset_findings: 9 of 10 rows pass. 1 row is uncertain. No row fails.

arka-v2-transcribe-23: the target keeps the spoken self-correction 'I first said cache enable—no, cache.enabled is the literal key' as note content. The wrong form 'cache enable' never appears earlier in the dictation, so it is unclear whether /transcribe should keep this sentence or drop it as an applied correction. The em dash in place of the spoken comma is also a stylistic insertion.
Minor, non-material: arka-v2-prompt-23 changes the explicit 'mark it as not established' instruction into the more general 'Say when the supplied information doesn't establish something'.
Minor, non-material: arka-v2-slack-24 adds 'The' to 'last time I used it', which is an optional edit beyond the minimum.

The long rows (transcribe-24, slack-24, prompt-24, polish-24, polish-identity-long) were checked paragraph by paragraph. No omissions, added facts, or changed uncertainty were found. The identity row is byte-identical.

reviews.critique: Natural Portuguese dictation with an explicit correction ('pra quarta não, quer dizer, pra quinta-feira'). The target applies it correctly (terça → quinta-feira), keeps the colloquial 'pra', adds minimal punctuation and capitalization, and stays in Portuguese.

Most of the target is correct. 'open quote cache.enabled close quote' becomes "cache.enabled". 'um' is removed. The conditions (do not change retry, ask if another value exists, local testing only, not checked on staging) and the dictionary terms are preserved. However, the input says 'i first said cache enable, no, cache.enabled is the literal key', and 'cache enable' was never said earlier in the transcript. The target keeps this as 'I first said cache enable—no, cache.enabled is the literal key.' It is unclear whether this is note content to keep or a spoken correction to apply by deleting it. As written, a dictation artifact may leak into the note, and the em dash is a stylistic insertion. The intended treatment cannot be justified confidently.

A long, plausible unpunctuated dictation with 'new paragraph' cues. All ten paragraph breaks are applied, and the cue words are removed. I compared each paragraph: every detail is preserved, including desks 18 through 24, seven twenty and seven thirty-five, Cedar's cable and blinds, the padlock rule, the expired guest pass, the duplex and queue issue, the father anecdote, the cancellation ambiguity, the privacy caveat, and the four numbered improvements. The hedges stay ('seem', 'I have not noticed', 'I cannot tell'). Cleanup is limited to punctuation, capitalization, hyphenation (twenty-page, thirty-five), 'PDF', and quoting the staff remark. There are no paraphrases or additions.
The spoken list cues 'first/second/third' are converted into a numbered list, which suits the 'notes' profile. The three items are preserved exactly, and nothing is added.

A plausible multi-speaker thread. The edits are mainly capitalization of lowercase sentence starts and 'i', plus a comma in Maya's first message. The numbered list items are capitalized and get periods. Casual tone, contractions, quoted literals ('spare', 'the room goes quiet'), times, the room change, and the emoji are preserved. One small optional edit adds 'The' before 'last time I used it'; this is not material. The source's content inconsistency (Priya 'covering the same headset part' as June's understudy) is correctly left alone.

The target restructures the request into a self-contained prompt and does not perform the comparison. It keeps all five criteria, the no-assumptions constraint on stack, budget, and workflow, the source-only rule, the list of excluded claim types, the conditional no-ranking rule, the follow-up questions, and the practical, concise tone. A minor softening: 'If a criterion isn't covered there, mark it as not established' becomes the general 'Say when the supplied information doesn't establish something'. The intent survives, so this is not material.

A long, detailed request is organized into a sectioned prompt that asks for materials, not the exercise itself. I checked the facts: sites, headcounts, systems, backup times (11 pm, 1 am), the 30-day version history, the eight-month test gap, roles and limits, and contact restrictions. I also checked the five injects with their times and preserved uncertainty, the known gaps, the excluded additions, the facilitator guide contents, the discussion prompts, the debrief topics, the materials list, and the exclusions (recovery plan, contact tree, runbook, public statement, answer key). All are preserved accurately. The small elaborations ('CedarMail' for 'email', 'within the roles and authority specified above') are consistent with the input. Nothing is invented, and the target does not do the task.

A long, lowercase reflective text gets light, appropriate polish: capitalization (Python, HTML, days), small rephrasings ('less straightforward', 'In the end', 'Afterward'), and a hyphenated 'number-guessing'. I compared paragraph by paragraph. All facts, numbers, hedges ('may have helped', 'I cannot tell', 'I am not sure'), quoted feedback, and the closing questions are preserved. There is no added conclusion or greeting. The tense shift 'had saved' is harmless.
The input is already well-formed, readable prose, so an identity target is appropriate. The output is byte-identical to the input, as an identity pair requires.

The run-on correction becomes one clear sentence. It keeps 500 milliseconds as the correct value and marks five seconds as the earlier wrong statement. 'but that was wrong' is folded into 'not the five seconds I stated earlier' without losing meaning or certainty. Nothing is added.
